checks.name: Dividend in AIS not declared
checks.description: AIS shows dividend income (SFT-015) that is not present in the taxpayer's draft return under Other Sources.
checks.plain_language: The tax department already knows about a dividend you received (from your broker/RTA) but your return currently shows Rs 0 for it.
checks.remedy: Add the dividend amount under 'Income from Other Sources' -> 'Dividend' before filing.

checks.name: Interest in AIS not declared
checks.description: AIS shows savings/FD interest that is not present in the draft return.
checks.plain_language: Your bank reported interest paid to you, but it's missing from your return.
checks.remedy: Add the interest amount under Other Sources; claim 80TTA/80TTB if eligible and using the old regime.

checks.name: TDS claimed exceeds Form 26AS
checks.description: The TDS amount claimed in the return is higher than what is reflected in Form 26AS for the same deductor/section.
checks.plain_language: You're asking for credit for more tax already deducted than the department's records show was actually deposited.
checks.remedy: Reconcile with Form 26AS; if a deductor hasn't deposited/reported TDS yet, follow up with them before filing, or claim only the reflected amount.

checks.name: Standard deduction claimed twice
checks.description: Multiple Form 16s each show a full standard deduction; only one standard deduction is allowed per assessee per year.
checks.plain_language: You changed jobs, and both employers each gave you the full Rs 50,000/75,000 standard deduction -- but you're only allowed to claim it once in total.
checks.remedy: When combining salary from multiple employers, apply the standard deduction only once in the consolidated Salary schedule.

checks.name: Refund bank account not prevalidated
checks.description: No bank account linked to the PAN is prevalidated and nominated for refund.
checks.plain_language: Even if you're owed a refund, the department can't pay it into an account that hasn't been verified on the portal.
checks.remedy: Go to 'My Bank Account' on the e-filing portal, add the account, and complete prevalidation before or right after filing.

checks.name: Capital gains present but ITR-1 selected
checks.description: Taxpayer has capital gains (STCG/LTCG) but has selected or drafted ITR-1, which does not support capital gains reporting.
checks.plain_language: ITR-1 is the simplest form, but it cannot be used at all if you sold any shares or mutual fund units at a gain -- you must use ITR-2.
checks.remedy: Switch to ITR-2 (or ITR-3 if you also have business income) and report gains in the Capital Gains schedule.

checks.name: Return not e-Verified
checks.description: Return has been filed but not yet e-Verified within the 30-day window.
checks.plain_language: Filing isn't the last step -- an unverified return is treated as if it was never filed at all after 30 days.
checks.remedy: e-Verify immediately via Aadhaar OTP, net banking, or by sending a signed ITR-V to CPC Bengaluru.

checks.name: PAN not linked with Aadhaar
checks.description: PAN is inoperative because it has not been linked to Aadhaar.
checks.plain_language: If your PAN and Aadhaar aren't linked, your PAN becomes inoperative and you cannot file or get refunds processed.
checks.remedy: Link PAN-Aadhaar on the e-filing portal (fee may apply) before filing.

checks.name: HRA exemption claimed under new regime
checks.description: HRA exemption (section 10(13A)) claimed while new tax regime is selected; not permitted under the new regime.
checks.plain_language: HRA exemption is an old-regime-only benefit -- it can't be claimed if you've opted for the new regime.
checks.remedy: Either switch to the old regime to claim HRA, or remove the HRA claim if staying in the new regime.

checks.name: Wrong interest deduction section for age
checks.description: Taxpayer aged 60+ claims 80TTA (max Rs 10,000, savings interest only) instead of the more generous 80TTB (max Rs 50,000, all bank/post office interest) available to senior citizens.
checks.plain_language: If you're 60 or older, you get a bigger interest deduction (80TTB, up to Rs 50,000, includes FD interest) -- don't limit yourself to the smaller 80TTA.
checks.remedy: Use 80TTB instead of 80TTA when the taxpayer is 60 or older and has chosen the old regime.

checks.name: LTCG 112A exceeds exemption
checks.description: Long-term capital gains on listed equity/equity MF (section 112A) exceed the Rs 1,25,000 annual exemption.
checks.plain_language: The first Rs 1,25,000 of long-term gains on shares/equity funds each year is tax-free; anything above that is taxed at 12.5%.
checks.remedy: No remedy needed -- just ensure the exemption is applied correctly and only the excess is taxed.

checks.name: 87A rebate wrongly applied to capital gains tax
checks.description: Section 87A rebate has been applied to reduce tax computed on STCG (111A) or LTCG (112A), which is not permitted even if total income is within the rebate threshold.
checks.plain_language: The 'up to Rs 12L = zero tax' rebate does not cover tax on gains from selling shares/mutual funds -- that portion is taxed regardless of your total income.
checks.remedy: Recompute rebate to apply only to tax on slab-rate (non-capital-gains) income.

checks.name: 194J stipend -- ITR form ambiguity
checks.description: Income received with 194J TDS looks like an internship/training stipend rather than genuine independent professional income.
checks.plain_language: Your stipend had 'professional fees' tax deducted, but you weren't really running an independent profession -- there's a genuine choice of how to report this.
checks.remedy: Report as Other Sources (ITR-1, simplest) or as presumptive professional income u/s 44ADA (ITR-4) -- either can be defensible; pick one and stay consistent for future references to this income.

checks.name: GST registration check for freelancers
checks.description: Freelancer/professional gross receipts are below the Rs 20,00,000 GST registration threshold for services.
checks.plain_language: You don't need to register for GST as long as your total professional receipts stay under Rs 20 lakh a year.
checks.remedy: No action needed unless receipts approach the threshold; monitor annually.

checks.name: Gross receipts exceed AIS/26AS total
checks.description: Taxpayer's actual gross receipts (per invoices) exceed the amount reflected in AIS/26AS because some clients did not deduct or report TDS.
checks.plain_language: AIS only shows income where someone deducted TDS and reported it -- cash or no-TDS clients won't show up, but you must still declare all your income.
checks.remedy: Maintain your own invoice/receipt records and declare total gross receipts, not just the AIS figure.

checks.name: TDS well below computed tax liability
checks.description: Total TDS credited is materially lower than the computed final tax liability, often due to multiple employers/payers each under-withholding independently.
checks.plain_language: Each of your employers only withheld tax as if you earned that much from them alone -- combined, you likely owe more tax than was deducted.
checks.remedy: Compute self-assessment tax due and pay it (Challan 280) before filing to avoid interest u/s 234B/234C.

checks.name: Old-regime-by-default assumption for seniors
checks.description: Senior citizen defaults to old regime assuming 80TTB makes it automatically better, without comparing to the new regime's higher rebate threshold.
checks.plain_language: Even senior citizens should compute both regimes -- the new regime's Rs 12 lakh rebate threshold can outweigh losing old-regime deductions like 80TTB.
checks.remedy: Always run both computations before choosing a regime, regardless of age-based deductions available.

checks.name: No Form 16 issued for this income
checks.description: No Form 16 is available for some or all income (e.g. professional fees, pension without employer, freelance receipts); rely on AIS/26AS and own records.
checks.plain_language: Not every kind of income comes with a Form 16 -- for freelance, stipend, or pension income, check AIS/26AS and your own payment records instead.
checks.remedy: Cross-check income figures against bank statements/invoices in addition to AIS/26AS.

checks.name: Pre-31-Jan-2018 equity holdings need grandfathered cost
checks.description: Equity/equity MF units acquired before 31-Jan-2018 must use the higher of actual cost and FMV as on 31-Jan-2018 (capped at sale value) as the cost of acquisition for LTCG.
checks.plain_language: For old share/mutual fund holdings bought before 31 Jan 2018, the taxable gain is calculated using a special 'grandfathered' cost, not just your original purchase price.
checks.remedy: Use the FMV as on 31-Jan-2018 (if higher than actual cost, capped at sale price) when computing LTCG for such holdings.

checks.name: Simplified/regional-language UI needed
checks.description: Taxpayer profile indicates low digital literacy and/or a preference for a regional language UI.
checks.plain_language: Some filers will need a simpler, guided experience in their preferred language rather than the standard flow.
checks.remedy: Route to a simplified/guided flow with Hindi (or other regional language) UI and larger-format prompts.

checks.name: Salary reported separately per employer in AIS
checks.description: AIS shows separate salary/TDS entries per employer (section 192); these need manual consolidation into one Salary schedule.
checks.plain_language: If you had two jobs in the year, AIS lists each employer's payment separately -- you must combine them yourself when filling in your return.
checks.remedy: Add both employers as separate rows within the same Salary schedule in the ITR form; apply standard deduction only once overall.
